_comment: FC-1 INC-4 decisive gate, SPLIT arm.  50-station GPS+Galileo golden posture, 3 h.
epoch_decimation_n = 2: a FULL solve every 60 s, a clocks-only fast TICK every 30 s,
n=2 rather than the SPEC's n=10.  At n=10 the full solve runs at 300 s spacing, which
is a measured carry-collapse regime (33%/ep refloat, arc life ~15 min, SH runaway at
hr 4) — a verdict there would confound 'the fast tier works' with 'the full solve
degraded'.  At 60 s the full solve is in the validated tier (D5 184/ep, sigma0 1.00),
so the only thing under test is the fast tier.  The ZOH floor to beat is correspondingly
REF arm: runs/fc1_shadow_3h/products.txt — the same build, same data, same posture at
epoch_decimation_n = 1.  Using the shadow run as REF is legitimate precisely because
the INC-0/INC-1 isolation gate proved its estimation outputs byte-identical to the
tier-off arm; shadow ticks are computed and discarded.
